programme.desc: Ben Garrod uncovers the secrets of how vertebrates capture and devour their food using extreme jaws, bizarre teeth and specialised bony tools. He takes a cherry picker up a sperm whale's jaw and finds out which animal has teeth weighing five kilos each and which uses its skull as a suction pump. Ben gets his own skull scanned and 3D-printed to discover how diet in humans isn't just affecting our waistlines but is also changing the shape of our bones.

programme.title: Ancient Worlds
programme.desc: In Richard Miles's epic story of civilization, there have been plenty of examples of the great men of history, but none came close to the legend of Alexander of Macedon, known to us as 'the Great'. Uniting the fractious Greek city-states, he led them on a crusade against the old enemy, Persia, and in little more than a decade created an empire that stretched from Egypt in the west to Afghanistan in the east. But it was Alexander's successors, the Hellenistic Kings, who had to make sense of the legacy of this charismatic adventurer. By knuckling down to the hard graft of politics, taxation and public works, they created something far more enduring than a mere legend - they built a civilization. Richard traces Alexander's battle-scarred route through Turkey, Syria and Lebanon to Egypt and ultimately to the western Punjab, Pakistan, where he discovers fascinating traces of a city where Greek west and Buddhist east were united in an intriguing new way.

programme.desc: Mark Radcliffe introduces this archive tribute to the Queen of Disco, who died in 2012. As a singer, Donna Summer had many strings to her bow as this compilation shows. programme.title: Disco: Soundtrack of a Revolution
programme.desc: In 1970s, in the aftermath of the Stonewall Riots, a sense of liberation fuelled a new sound from New York. In their quest for a safe space to meet – free from discrimination and violence – New York’s gay, black and minority ethnic communities started coming together in apartments and basement bars to dance. It was the beginning of a new kind of music and a pioneering dance floor culture that would sweep the world and change dance music forever.

programme.title: Black British Music at the BBC
programme.desc: DJ Spoony takes a musical journey that showcases the artists, songs and genres that have done so much to shape the nation’s musical landscape over the years – from old school right up to the present. Spoony has personally selected a playlist of 40 great tracks that bring together some of the most inspiring names from the worlds of pop, soul, ska, reggae, rap and garage - and finds the likes of Seal, The Selecter and Soul II Soul rubbing shoulders with FKA Twigs, Miss Dynamite and Dame Shirley Bassey. Spoony also celebrates the rich vein of collaboration that runs through so much Black British music, sharing songs and performances from acts, including Wretch 32 and Shola Ama, Loyle Carner and Jorja Smith, Little Simz and Cleo Sol, and Tinie Tempah and Labrinth.

programme.title: Natural World
programme.desc: Seals, parakeets and even pelicans that eat pigeons have all made London their home. That's as well as badgers, foxes, scorpions, and pigeons that ride the tube. But even more wonderful are the people who love the exotic wildlife of our capital, from Billingsgate fish porters and Indian chefs to 'Crayfish Bob', who scours London's canals for Turkish invaders. This is a warm-hearted portrait of the world's greenest capital city and the Londoners who love its secret wildlife.

programme.title: Full Circle with Michael Palin
programme.desc: Michael Palin travels around the Pacific rim. He starts in the Diomede Islands in the Bering Strait, goes to see the Kodiak bear in Alaska and visits the geysers and hot springs of Kamchatka.

programme.title: Talking Pictures
programme.desc: In 2025, when Christopher Nolan was preparing to shoot The Odyssey, it was a film made 40 years earlier that he screened for his team to help inspire them. That film was Ran, directed by one of the true giants of world cinema, Akira Kurosawa. Kurosawa is one of five directors whose work is explored in this celebration of international films. Celia Imrie shares interviews and key moments from the BBC's rich archives to look at his work and the work of four other greats who shared his vision and passion for film - Agnes Varda, Francois Truffaut, Luis Buñuel and Ingmar Bergman. We see how they and their groundbreaking, inspirational films changed the language of world cinema and showed those who came after them exactly what the movie camera is capable of achieving.

programme.title: BBC Young Musician
programme.desc: Presented by Petroc Trelawny, BBC Young Musician reaches the crucial quarter-final stage. Just eight musicians remain, and each are out to impress the judges and claim that allimportant place in the semi-final. Star pianist and recording artist Joanna MacGregor and conductor and broadcaster Ben Gernon return to their seats on the judging panel. Joining them as guest judge is one of the world’s leading clarinettists, Julian Bliss. Having burst onto the classical music scene at a young age, he knows only too well how it feels to perform at the highest standard. Filmed at Swansea University’s Great Hall, this programme features highlights from a thrilling quarter-final and includes music by JS Bach, Prokofiev, Debussy and more. With such talent on display, it’s not going to be an easy decision for the judges. Which five musicians will they decide to put through to the semi-final?

programme.title: Shakespeare: Rise of a Genius
programme.desc: 1587. William Shakespeare leaves the small rural town of Stratford to pursue his dreams of becoming a playwright in the dangerous, growing metropolis of London. Public theatre is red-hot modernity, and Shakespeare begins his journey at the very bottom. Inspired by the live fast, die young world he inhabits, he writes the schlock horror hit Titus Andronicus and a teenage romance where all the young people die: Romeo and Juliet.

programme.title: Remembers...
programme.desc: Dame Helen Mirren looks back on one of her earliest television roles, filmed before she’d become a household name and international star, playing Rosalind in the BBC’s 1978 production of the Shakespeare comedy As You Like It. She shares her thoughts on the potential that As You Like It’s playing with gender could have for today’s audiences, reflects on the quality of the roles Shakespeare wrote for women and explains why she thinks the Bard will be as significant in 100 years’ time as he is today.

programme.title: The BBC Television Shakespeare
programme.desc: A set of television adaptations of all 37 plays by William Shakespeare.

programme.title: Shakespeare in Italy
programme.desc: Francesco da Mosto takes a look at Italy as the land of adventure and ambition - where fortunes are made and battles are fought. Beginning in Venice with actor Ciaran Hinds, Francesco considers how his home town so renowned for its justice struck Shakespeare as the perfect setting for his disturbing tale of what happens to an outsider who goes against the law in The Merchant of Venice. Heading south to Rome, Francesco discovers how in his great Roman plays Julius Caesar and Antony and Cleopatra, Shakespeare used this ancient city as a smokescreen to address the most burning political issues of his day while avoiding trouble with the Elizabethan censors. Francesco meets Shakespearean actor Mark Rylance, and also pops in to Rome's very own Globe to understand modern Italy's fascination with our English Bard. Finally he travels from Naples to the beautiful Island of Stromboli, just off the north coast of Sicily, a magical setting for Shakespeare's final great masterpiece - The Tempest.

programme.title: Clive Myrie's African Adventure
programme.desc: Clive’s final destination in South Africa is a place he never grows tired of – Cape Town. It’s one of South Africa’s three capitals, and it has perhaps the best views of any city on the planet. While he’s there, Clive serves lunch to the waddling residents of the city’s penguin rehab centre and discovers how the team nurses sick penguins back to health. He heads to the candy-coloured houses of the city’s famous Bo-Kaap district to learn the flavour-packed art of Cape Malay cooking, and he feeds his passion for jazz by joining a jam with up-and-coming singer-songwriter Q Ntshinka. Finally, he gets a lesson in the art of trapeze with the multicultural crew of the Zip Zap Circus.

programme.title: The Climate Question
programme.desc: A global programme that reflects the variety of takes on climate change, how best to understand it and the world's attempts to avert it, temper it or adapt to it. It is not about questioning whether climate change is happening, it's about finding the best ways to respond to it. This is sharp-edged, analytical inquiry. Hard scrutiny, touched with a sense of adventure and discovery, and where we can find it, hope. It includes stories from across the world on why we find it so hard to save our own planet, and how we might change that.

programme.desc: Writer and producer Russell T Davies reflects on his career, from the groundbreaking series Queer as Folk to the revival of Doctor Who, Years and Years and his latest Channel 4 drama Tip Toe. The BBC has issued an apology for making false and defamatory allegations about the founder of PinkNews and his husband. programme.title: The Travel Show
programme.desc: As the Welsh towns of Port Talbot and Pontypridd compete to be the UK's first-ever Town of Culture, Rob Bell explores southern Wales to find out what the title would mean for these formerly industrial areas. Rob attends a 850-year-old celebration of Welsh culture, rides in a rollercoaster in an abandoned colliery now revived by the miners who used to work there, and even goes swimming with sharks in an effort to find out if the country's natural treasures could be used in a different way for the benefit of future generations.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: The latest news from the BBC.

programme.title: AI Decoded
programme.desc: AI Decoded looks ahead to the release of major new film, Artificial, which reignites one of the most important debates in technology. The controversial drama explores the growing divide between OpenAI co-founders Sam Altman and Ilya Sutskever, and a question that now sits at the centre of the AI revolution: should we accelerate the development of ever more powerful AI systems, or slow down before the risks become unmanageable? The debate comes as concerns over AI security continue to grow. In the same week that Ukrainian attacks reportedly targeted Russian data centre infrastructure, the UK's AI minister warned that AI-assisted cyber attacks are becoming increasingly likely. Meanwhile, MI5 says terrorists are already attempting to exploit artificial intelligence. Joining Marc Cieslak and Dr Stephanie Hare are technology futurist Bernard Marr and AI safety researcher Roman Yampolskiy, one of the world's leading voices on the risks posed by superintelligent AI.

programme.title: Global Eye
programme.desc: A weekly programme from the BBC World Service, bringing forensic journalism from all corners of the world by BBC Eye, the World Service's critically acclaimed investigative unit, and featuring expert global correspondents getting to the heart of the biggest international stories. In this episode: Nadine Yousif reports from Canada, where growing tensions over Alberta's place within the federation are fuelling a debate about identity, sovereignty and political power. As some push for greater autonomy and others warn against deepening divisions, Global Eye examines competing visions of Canada's future. Plus: we travel to the remote mountains of Papua, where the world's last tropical glaciers are rapidly disappearing, exploring what their loss means for Indigenous communities and a landscape undergoing profound change.

programme.title: Crimewatch Live
programme.desc: How detectives jailed the owner of an XL bully dog that killed a much-loved grandmother. And can you help put a name to an unknown deceased man?

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Programme in which experts uncover the various tricks of the property auction trade

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Traditional ceramics get a modern twist when Natasha Raskin Sharp meets artist Lucy Bryant, who uses a technique called bricolage to breathe new life into forgotten plates and figurines. At Ardingly antiques fair, experts Caroline Hawley and Thomas Forrester are ready to host two more teams on a dash around the stalls. Hunting for jewellery are Vijoo and her husband, Conny. Shopping against them are partners James and George, who plan to spend big right away. While the lads gallop off in search of George’s favourite animal, a horse, Vijoo and Conny prefer a leisurely trot. Twenty minutes later, they’re still pondering their first purchase. For the auction, the teams travel to Chichester, where the experts reveal their bonus buys. Thomas sticks with a familiar theme, while Caroline brings a touch of Scandi style to the proceedings.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Sister Boniface Mysteries
programme.desc: When the church cleaner is poisoned during Felix and Victoria's wedding rehearsal, Sister Boniface and Sam need to investigate the guests from Bermuda.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: It’s an island escape as Jules Hudson helps a couple from a town in Cheshire to find their dream home on Anglesey. During a busy week of house hunting, Jules turns his attention away from property and heads to the Welsh mainland to catch up with a passionate farmer, Gareth Wyn Jones, whose family has been working the land for 375 years.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Charlie and Flo travel to Stourbridge to help Vicki and Mark transform their barren garden into a stunning bumblebee haven. With only a towering copper beech tree to work around, the couple dream of creating a stylish and welcoming outdoor retreat for dining, entertaining and relaxation. Inspired by their family trip to Greece, they want a garden that brings everyone together, including their eldest son, Alex, while honouring the memory of Vicki’s mum with bumblebees and Mark’s mum with a cherished sculpture from her garden. With open space for the whole family, including dogs Lola and Minnie, and a budget of just £3,500, can Charlie and Flo deliver a garden that’s both beautiful and deeply personal?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp hosts the high-stakes quiz as celebrities TV presenter and Olympian Sam Quek, ex-footballer and TV presenter Dion Dublin, actress and TV presenter Joanna Page and radio DJ Melvin Odoom attempt to cross the Bridge of Lies and win money for their chosen charities. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and 10 lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money, step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge, they just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash for their chosen charities.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Andi Oliver for the brainy quiz where the contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

Each week, a stellar cast of celebrity guests reveal extraordinary stories about themselves. But are they telling the truth, or are they making it all up? Sorting the fact from fiction this time are guests Lucy Beaumont, Frankie Boyle, Abby Cook and Mo Gilligan.

programme.desc: The search for the UK’s Next Drag Race Superstar continues. programme.title: Mary at 90: A Lifetime of Cooking
programme.desc: Bringing her friends together to share delicious dinner party dishes has been a highlight of Mary's cooking life. While the style of dinner parties has changed over 60 years, the joy brought from gathering friends to eat good food is still alive and kicking. Actor Kiell Smith-Bynoe also loves to host, but he is more at home making the cocktails than the food. So Mary is coming to the rescue with four impressive but simple recipes: porcini mushroom arancini with a melted dolcelatte centre, roast salmon with parmesan crust and creamy mushroom and wine sauce, fillet tails of beef with a rich bearnaise sauce, and chocolate roulade with raspberry coulis. Mary and Kiell cook up a storm for his friends, and Kiell shares his life-long passion for magic with his dinner guests and a very enthusiastic Mary.

programme.title: The Football Interview
programme.desc: The Football Interview sees the biggest names in sport and entertainment join host Kelly Somers for bold, in-depth conversations about the nation’s favourite sport. We explore mindset and motivation, reflect on defining moments and career highs, and discuss personal insights. It’s a chance to show an honest, human and sometimes surprising side to familiar faces. At the heart of this is Kelly Somers – one of the most trusted, versatile and authentic voices in sports broadcasting. Kelly brings a brand of warmth and relatability that resonates with both athletes and audiences. What sets her apart is her ability to dig deeper with a sensitive approach, creating a space where athletes feel comfortable being open, honest and at times vulnerable. Each episode sees Kelly draw out stories and insight from the player behind the name about the beautiful game, their origins and values, and a look-ahead to the future from a sporting and personal perspective. She takes her subjects on a journey – and takes the viewer with her.

Alan brushes up on his culinary skills, learning how to cook the classic Italian dish ravioli with local friend Luca, and Amanda brings a touch of colour to the kitchen, covering the fireplace in handmade tiles. Keen to source local Carrara marble for their worktops, the duo visit an active quarry in the Apuan Alps but face a treacherous journey to get there. Elizabeth and Margaret envision a charming pergola draped in delicate vines, offering a peaceful spot to unwind together. Wider, gently sloping steps and accessible raised beds will allow Margaret to continue her beloved gardening safely, while lush, in-ground plants reduce maintenance. They also hope for privacy screening and planting that discreetly hides the shed at the back of the garden. Elizabeth juggles a demanding full-time job with caring for her ageing mother, leaving little time to work on the garden. Margaret is retired and longing to enjoy the outdoors, but her partial sight makes the current low-lying plants and treacherous steps a real obstacle to relaxation and upkeep. Can the team turn this challenging plot into a peaceful mother–daughter retreat on a £4,500 budget?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents this quiz show where a team of four friends, Louise, Mark, Suzy and Rich, take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Wilderness with Simon Reeve
programme.desc: Simon Reeve journeys deep into Canada’s vast and empty Yukon territory – one of North America’s most iconic and remote landscapes. Covering an area almost the size of Spain but home to fewer than 50,000 people, the Yukon is a land of immense forests, glaciers, rivers and wildlife. In wealthy, modern Canada, Simon wants to find out how the people and the wildlife of this immense wilderness are faring - all while searching for an apex predator, the grizzly bear.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Political Thinking with Nick Robinson
programme.desc: Nick Robinson in conversation with people who influence our political thinking.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: Game show presented by Rick Edwards in which players score points by answering questions correctly. However, they must avoid the Impossible answers, otherwise they will be eliminated from the show until the next day. In each episode, there are three rounds, and the three highest scorers from each round play against each other in the final. The winner of this battle faces a £10,000 question.

programme.title: The Answer Run
programme.desc: Comedian Jason Manford hosts an exciting, fast-paced quiz show where three couples face a series of 50/50 questions which hurtle the Answer Run down towards them. Across three rounds, the couples build up their cash pots, but only one pair can face the Final Run and win the chance to take home their cash prize. Who will swipe their way to victory?

programme.title: The Boss
programme.desc: Susan Calman hosts the quiz show of tactics, knowledge and nerve. Contestants must work as a team, but ultimately there can only be one Boss. Who will pick off their opponents and walk away with the thousands of pounds on offer?

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael concludes his journey from Cumbria to Dumfriesshire by crossing the Solway Firth into Scotland, where he visits the beautifully preserved last home of Scotland’s greatest poet, Robert Burns. At his mausoleum, he reflects on Burns’s enduring legacy before enjoying one of his songs performed in the Scots language. Further north into the Lowther Hills, Michael strikes gold in the rich geological landscape around Wanlockhead, Scotland’s highest village, and rides a charming heritage industrial railway across the stunning terrain. The journey ends at the spectacular Palladian mansion of Dumfries House, home to a world-class Chippendale furniture collection and the headquarters of the King’s Foundation. In a traditional skills workshop, Michael discovers why he was never destined to be a builder.

programme.title: The Great House Revival
programme.desc: Architects Fiona and Paddy found an abandoned cow house deep in a forest. As they relocate from Dublin, can they transform this unusual ruin into their family's dream home?

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel and the team head for Hampton Court, uncovering more treasures. Amongst the valuables coming to light are a bronze produced by Rodin, an early longcase clock and a sketch by abstract artist Mondrian valued at over £50,000.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Paul Martin presents from Ragley Hall in Warwickshire, a beautiful 17th-century Palladian house owned by the Marquess of Hertford. Antiques experts Charlie Ross and Will Axon find great treasures among hundreds of visitors to the stately home. Charlie models an interesting busby hat and Will gets a surprise when a Worcester coffee set goes under the hammer. Meanwhile, Paul explores the Battle of Edgehill.

programme.title: House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Chizzy Akudolu, Stephen Bailey, Banjo Beale, and Philippa Dunne take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, Michael Sheen. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted with the brand new House of Games record player?

programme.title: Strictly - It Takes Two
programme.desc: Ellie Taylor is on hand with more behind-the-scenes action and is joined by a trio of Strictly all-stars to discuss all things ballroom. Plus, more exclusive interviews with some of the remaining celebrities.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the crucial news stories of the day. With Matt Chorley.

programme.title: Landward
programme.desc: Dougie is in the Borders to round up all the action from the Sheep Dog World Trial at Lauder. He finds out how the family hosting the event turned their working farm into a championship venue and also meets some of the international competitors taking part with their dogs. Rosie is on Bute for a trialling masterclass from one of the sport’s best handlers, Cammy is at the Kelso Ram Sales to investigate the continuing decline in sheep numbers in Scotland, and Anne visits the craftswoman keeping the tradition of crook making alive.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Frances Tophill is tackling jobs in the autumn garden and introduces plants that keep colour and interest going for as long as possible. She plants garlic in containers and perennial vegetables into the border - delicious veg that comes back year after year with very little effort. She also has some great propagation tips for creating plants for free. Jamie Butterworth delves into the fascinating world of shade-loving plants, revealing the remarkable range of colours, textures and forms that can flourish away from the sun. Ashley Edwards joins sound artist Jason Singh for an unusual journey through the garden, exploring the hidden sounds of plants. A couple have designed a garden around an elaborate miniature railway, and there’s an extraordinary collection of lithops, otherworldly succulents known as living stones.

programme.title: Six Wives with Lucy Worsley
programme.desc: This episode follows the end of Henry's marriage to Katherine of Aragon, made possible by Henry's rejection of Catholicism and the pope, with him setting himself up as head of the Church of England. He marries his second wife, Anne Boleyn, and she gives birth to a baby girl, Elizabeth. After rumours spread that Anne has been unfaithful to the king, she is arrested and executed, leaving Henry free to marry Jane Seymour. Jane gives birth to a son, Edward, but Henry's joy is overshadowed by grief as Jane dies 12 days later.

programme.title: The Silence of the Lambs
programme.desc: FBI trainee Clarice Starling, enticing insights from confined killer Hannibal Lecter, shares her nightmare memory in the hope of stopping a serial killer before his latest victim dies.

programme.title: In Fabric
programme.desc: Comedy horror. Bank cashier Sheila is determined to make an impression on a blind date, and she is persuaded to buy a stunning red dress from an intimidating department store. Little does she know just what effect that dress will have.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: Roman Abramovich was the Russian oligarch who brought his wealth to the UK. But what’s the truth about Roman Abramovich’s fortune? Working with the Bureau of Investigative Journalism, Panorama investigates the documents that were falsified to hide his wealth and evade tax. Roman Abramovich's lawyers say he denies evading tax or concealing his fortune.

programme.title: Time
programme.desc: Officer Bailey faces a moral crossroads after tragedy strikes HMYOI Alderwick, whilst Marie-Louise and the governor deliver some news to family on the outside. James, consumed by shame, learns a truth and debates facing family he has been avoiding. Peter’s guilt inside grows, and he forms an unlikely connection. Pressure hits a critical high at the prison as officers and prisoners alike struggle to cope.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Piripenguins
programme.desc: The Piris find a skeleton buried in the ice and think it’s an ancient ancestor. But after a series of strange discoveries, things take an unexpected turn.

programme.title: Big Lizard
programme.desc: Dad gets a severe case of Proximan hiccups. Big Lizard and Cosima do their best to help, but their attempt to scare Dad goes wrong when a real 'monster' turns up!

programme.title: The Weasy Family
programme.desc: Weasy teams up with the cheating Chipmunk to win a game of basketball.

programme.title: Super Happy Magic Forest
programme.desc: The heroes are questing to find out who is behind a string of cake thefts, and go into detective mode. After questioning the baker, they decide to stage a stakeout at the bakery. However, when they spy cakes apparently walking off by themselves, they realise that there is more to this mystery than meets the eye - and a quest to find some missing cakes soon turns into a quest to save the entire forest!

programme.title: Grizzy and the Lemmings
programme.desc: Grizzy and the Lemmings fight over a silkworm.

programme.title: Duck and Frog
programme.desc: Duck is a ball boy at an important tennis match, but Frog causes chaos by accidentally filling the automatic ball launcher with oranges that splat the crowd!

programme.title: Pokémon Horizons
programme.desc: The Rising Volt Tacklers meet up with new and old friends at Blueberry Academy.

programme.title: Winx Club - The Magic Is Back
programme.desc: Following an accident, Tecna's magic is short-circuited, forcing her to come to terms with her emotions. The Winx and the Specialists take her to her home world of Zenith to be repaired.

programme.title: Blue Peter
programme.desc: Two super talented spaniels and one of the strongest women in the world attempt to smash world records in the studio. Shini attempts to clean the windows of the tallest building in the UK.

programme.title: Newsround
programme.desc: Topical news magazine for children.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Anita Rani and Sean Fletcher head to the south Pennines to join archaeologists and conservationists uncovering the remarkable ways peat is preserving our past while helping to protect our future. Meanwhile, John Craven reveals the winner of this year’s Countryfile photography competition for Children in Need.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Frances Tophill is tackling jobs in the autumn garden and introduces plants that keep colour and interest going for as long as possible. She plants garlic in containers and perennial vegetables into the border - delicious veg that comes back year after year with very little effort. She also has some great propagation tips for creating plants for free. Jamie Butterworth delves into the fascinating world of shade-loving plants, revealing the remarkable range of colours, textures and forms that can flourish away from the sun. Ashley Edwards joins sound artist Jason Singh for an unusual journey through the garden, exploring the hidden sounds of plants. A couple have designed a garden around an elaborate miniature railway, and there’s an extraordinary collection of lithops, otherworldly succulents known as living stones.

programme.title: Cycling: Track World Championships
programme.desc: Clare Balding presents live coverage from day 4 of the Track Cycling World Championships in Shanghai, with British medal hopes in the women’s madison and a world record expected in the emerging women’s 1km time trial event. Analysis comes from Laura Kenny. Plus a chance to catch up on the best of the action from the first three days of competition.

programme.title: North by Northwest
programme.desc: Classic Alfred Hitchcock thriller. When advertising executive Roger Thornhill is mistaken for the mysterious Mr Kaplan by a ruthless espionage ring, he soon faces deadly peril, framed for murder. On the run, Thornhill seeks Kaplan, the one person who can verify his story.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: The Museum of Science and Industry in Manchester is the fitting location for an episode full of wonder. Anita Manning and Michael Baggott value some extraordinary antiques, from high-quality Danish silver to a pot of gold that makes one local lady very happy indeed. Paul Martin takes an architectural tour of Manchester and checks out a replica of the first ever computer, designed and built in Manchester.

programme.title: Wilderness with Simon Reeve
programme.desc: Simon Reeve journeys deep into Canada’s vast and empty Yukon territory – one of North America’s most iconic and remote landscapes. Covering an area almost the size of Spain but home to fewer than 50,000 people, the Yukon is a land of immense forests, glaciers, rivers and wildlife. In wealthy, modern Canada, Simon wants to find out how the people and the wildlife of this immense wilderness are faring - all while searching for an apex predator, the grizzly bear.

programme.title: Where Eagles Dare
programme.desc: Seven paratroopers, led by a British intelligence officer, are sent on a seemingly impossible mission. They must enter an almost impregnable Nazi stronghold, the Castle of the Eagles, to rescue a high-ranking American officer. But the men's dangerous task is threatened by a traitor in the group.

programme.title: 40 Hits of 1986 at the BBC
programme.desc: Forty classic hits from 1986 taken from the BBC's archives. With Wham! wrapping things up, artists such as George Michael, Simply Red, Samantha Fox and Jermaine Stewart found success, while the synth sounds of bands like the Pet Shop Boys, A-ha, Eurythmics and Erasure were everywhere. But the charts still had plenty of room for lots more, including a musical bar of soap from Nick Berry with Every Loser Wins and plenty of Eurotrash in the form of Falco, Nana Mouskouri and even the band called Europe, blasting out their Final Countdown.

programme.title: Top of the Pops
programme.desc: Top of the Pops Big Hits is back with a bang for the year of 1986. Pop, new wave, rock, funk and R&B are all celebrated within this 60-minute special. The treasure troves of the BBC archives are open, so expect smoke machines, shoulder pads and perms along with studio performances from Bon Jovi, Cyndi Lauper, Cameo, The Pretenders, The Real Thing, Billy Ocean and The Communards. Other highlights include The Housemartins, Kim Wilde and The Human League plus The Cure and many more.

programme.title: Top of the Pops
programme.desc: How did the decline of the young guns of the early 80s, the advent of House, The Big Bang in the money markets and political fatigue on the Left make their mark - or not - on the nation’s most popular music show? Paul Heaton, Mick Hucknall, Sinitta, The Communards and Swing Out Sister are among the acts that steer us through the changes impacting Britain, the music industry and the BBC’s long-serving pop powerhouse in 1986.

programme.title: Saving Lives at Sea
programme.desc: A French yacht has made a mayday call after suffering mechanical failure near Jersey. The St Helier crew must rescue the vessel before it drifts onto a notoriously treacherous reef. In Porthcawl, when multiple 999 calls come in about a man who has been swept into the sea, the crew launch into the most dangerous conditions they’ve ever faced. Just along the south Wales coast, the Barry Dock lifeboat is tasked with two casualties on a remote island who have ingested hemlock: a poisonous plant that can be fatal. Across the Irish Sea, the crew are paged after reports come in of a swimmer in difficulty. And in Moelfre, north Wales, training night is interrupted by a dog owner whose beloved pet has jumped off a cliff.

programme.title: Finding Britain’s Slave Traders with David Olusoga
programme.desc: David Olusoga reveals how the end of the royal monopoly and the expansion of commerce was the 'big bang' moment in the story of the slave trade. In the 18th century, the trade in enslaved Africans would reach its peak as it expanded out of the royal court to provincial towns and ports across the country, with thousands of new investors.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Cycling: Track World Championships
programme.desc: Live coverage of the morning session on the final day of the Track Cycling World Championships in Shanghai in the company of Simon Brotherton and Chris Boardman. Featuring the early rounds of the women’s keirin and men’s sprint, including four-time Commonwealth gold medallist Emma Finucane.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Landward
programme.desc: Dougie is in the Borders to round up all the action from the Sheep Dog World Trial at Lauder. He finds out how the family hosting the event turned their working farm into a championship venue and also meets some of the international competitors taking part with their dogs. Rosie is on Bute for a trialling masterclass from one of the sport’s best handlers, Cammy is at the Kelso Ram Sales to investigate the continuing decline in sheep numbers in Scotland, and Anne visits the craftswoman keeping the tradition of crook making alive.

programme.title: Cycling: Track World Championships
programme.desc: Clare Balding presents continued live coverage of the final day of the Track Cycling World Championships in Shanghai, with the men’s sprint and British medal hopes in the women’s keirin in the shape of Commonwealth champion Emma Finucane. There are also the finals of the men’s elimination and women’s points race, with analysis from Laura Kenny.

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen Best Bites
programme.desc: Matt Tebbutt dishes up delicious flavours from around the world. Angela Hartnett kicks things off with an Italian classic - a rich egg yolk garganelli pasta tossed through a sausage and fennel ragu. Ollie Dabbous makes a mussel and monkfish bourride with a rich garlic aioli and plenty of crusty bread to dip into the sauce. Rachel Allen prepares her take on a shrimp gumbo - which isn’t really a gumbo at all - served with a chilli cornbread. Miguel Barclay has plenty of tips on how to maximise flavour whilst keeping costs down, while Ravneet Gill brings back a classic with her black forest gateau. Finally, Sara Cox tucks into either her food heaven, Mexican bean soup with fried tortillas, or her food hell, lemon sponge cake. Meanwhile, Rick Stein meets more of his food heroes, and the Hairy Bikers are in Catalonia, exploring the finest of vintages.

programme.title: Eva Longoria: Searching for France
programme.desc: Bordeaux’s world-famous vineyards are undergoing a revival as vintners seek to update their wines by introducing new technology and reinventing older traditions. Eva visits Saint-Emilion, where wine production began 1,000 years ago, and enjoys unusual wine pairings - a deep red with fish and a buttery white with cheese. But Bordeaux isn’t just about wine; it has superb produce, including succulent duck and tender beef as well as 200-million-year-old caviar, served with signature bordelaise sauces.

programme.title: The Colditz Story
programme.desc: Based on the true story from World War II of the notorious German POW establishment and the officers who tried to escape from it.

programme.title: Women's Super League
programme.desc: Manchester City play Brighton & Hove Albion in the Women's Super League.

programme.title: This Farming Life
programme.desc: New life is at the forefront of everyone’s mind, which means round-the-clock care for some. In Inverkip, after a successful pregnancy scan, Rachel and Camy are getting their sheds ready for the new crop of Park Cheviot Ewes – the best in their flock. They hope the ewes will give birth unaided, but they must stay vigilant in case they need to intervene. Nikki and Ollie welcome their first colony of rabbit kits as their breeding programme takes off. Things are looking up, but Ollie’s long hours at the maltings and the rise in cost of building materials mean their holiday pods are over budget and time. In the Cairngorms National Park, it’s out with the old and in with the new. Robert heads to market to sell previous year’s crop of spring calves – a nerve-wracking wait to find out what this year’s profit for a year’s hard work will be. Meanwhile, this year’s calves are due, so he’s up all hours ensuring each newborn is safely delivered.

programme.title: The Book That Changed My Life
programme.desc: Inspired by her passion to get people reading, Her Majesty Queen Camilla joins four remarkable people to share the stories of books that shaped them. Warm, emotional and full of hope, the film shows how reading can lift people up, open minds and even change lives in a celebration of the magic power inside every book.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Paul Martin presents from Wrest Park, a 19th-century French-style chateau surrounded by three centuries of English garden design in the Bedfordshire countryside. From the assembled crowd on the formal lawns, antiques experts Anita Manning and Christina Trevanion select the best antiques and collectibles to take to auction. Paul explores the grounds at Wrest, taking a look at the nationally significant collection of statuary and finding out about the key characters who made Wrest what it is today.

programme.title: Eva Longoria: Searching for France
programme.desc: Eva and her Breton guide Tanguy Thomassin explore the vast oyster beds of Cancale, oyster capital of Brittany. Being pummelled by one of the highest tides in Europe makes for fatter, sweeter and healthier oysters. And having once supplied King Louis XVI’s oyster habit, Brittany still supplies half of France. Bretons also boast of plentiful sardines, kelp forests, spiny crabs and the rare cobalt blue lobster. Fished sustainably and cooked on a grill, it's little wonder that this beauty is called the king of lobsters.

programme.title: The Balkans: Europe’s Forgotten Frontier
programme.desc: The BBC's Europe editor Katya Adler travels to Croatia, Bosnia and Albania. This is a corner of Europe that Katya first visited during the Yugoslav wars of independence. Thirty years later, she discovers a beautiful region that’s changing rapidly - but is also seen as the weak link of Europe, where Russia, China and the Islamic world are vying with the West for influence and power.

programme.title: Wilderness with Simon Reeve
programme.desc: Simon Reeve travels across Mongolia – the most sparsely populated country on Earth and home to some of the most brutal and beautiful landscapes on the planet. Six times the size of the UK but with fewer than 3.5 million people, Simon wants to find out how nomadic traditions, such as hunting with golden eagles, and wild nature still shape everyday life, all while searching for the elusive snow leopard.

programme.title: Later... with Jools Holland
programme.desc: Jools welcomes rock duo Royal Blood, drummer Moses Boyd, singer and DJ Shygirl, Irish folk group Kingfishr, cellist and singer Ayanna Witter-Johnson and the legendary Tony Iommi.

programme.title: Priscilla
programme.desc: Fourteen-year-old schoolgirl Priscilla Beaulieu is accustomed to the unsettled life of an army family. Invited to a party at Elvis Presley’s house as he carries out his military service in Germany, the shy teenager catches his eye and is gradually drawn into a strange and unhealthy codependent life. Based on Priscilla Presley’s autobiography.

programme.title: Question Time
programme.desc: Fiona Bruce presents an hour of debate from Brecon, with politicians, commentators and members of the public. On the panel: for Labour, the Welsh secretary Stephen Kinnock; the Conservatives’ shadow Welsh secretary Mims Davies; Plaid Cymru’s deputy minister for social care Delyth Jewell; Reform UK’s shadow health minister James Evans; and the journalist and author George Monbiot. Watch or listen first on the BBC News Channel, iPlayer and Sounds at 9pm.

programme.title: This is CBBC!
programme.desc: Tune every day from 7.00am.

programme.title: Shaun the Sheep
programme.desc: Bitzer thinks the Farmer is planning to replace him, so Shaun helps to knock his friend into shape. Unfortunately, Bitzer goes completely over the top with his training regime and starts running the farm with military precision, driving everyone crazy.

programme.title: Danger Mouse
programme.desc: A mishap on a mission leaves Danger Mouse confused - why is Penfold not talking to him? It might be because today is Penfold's birthday and he hasn't remembered it again! Squawk sprays DM with her experimental empathy gas in the hope that he will find it easier to care about other people. The newly empathetic DM is a changed mouse! One who seems to think breaking the Baron out of prison is a great idea.

programme.title: Super Happy Magic Forest
programme.desc: Mr Friendlyface is acting very strangely indeed. He refuses to stamp any of Admin Bunny’s documents, keeps getting distracted by butterflies, and seems oddly happy! The heroes are extremely suspicious and decide that someone must have swapped him with a doppelganger. Now they must quest to find out where the real Friendlyface is and get him back before the forest descends into total chaos.

programme.title: Boy Girl Dog Cat Mouse Cheese
programme.desc: Dog decides to show the family that he can be as tough as the wolves they are watching on TV. He joins a gang of street dogs and soon becomes leader of the pack. Meanwhile, the rest of the kids worry when Dog doesn’t come home and go out looking for him. However, they find that he is now too cool to be part of the 'old' family - until he is forced to make a choice between loyalty to the pack and loyalty to his best friend Boy.

programme.title: Newsround
programme.desc: Topical news magazine for children.

programme.title: Grizzy and the Lemmings
programme.desc: The Lemmings meet a parrot that can identically reproduce any sound.

programme.title: Grizzy and the Lemmings
programme.desc: The Lemmings discover a spherical object that can control Earth's rotation.

programme.title: SpongeBob SquarePants
programme.desc: SpongeBob tries to keep Fred's leg out of harm's way.

programme.title: Duck and Frog
programme.desc: When Duck and Frog get a job in a restaurant kitchen, Frog accidentally makes the soup incredibly spicy. He wants to serve it to a celebrity chef, but Duck wants to stop him!

programme.title: Duck and Frog
programme.desc: Duck is a tour guide at a grand stately home, and Frog thinks it's so nice that he decides to move in. When he gets annoyed by the tourists, Frog dresses up as a ghost to scare them off.

programme.title: Odd Squad
programme.desc: An international high-tech organisation run by kids, which investigates all things strange, weird and, most importantly, odd.

programme.title: Shark Bites
programme.desc: Steve Backshall meets the most ravenous shark in the sea, the tiger shark. Known for eating tin cans and even car number plates, these sharks are in fact perfectly honed hunters.

programme.title: Bitesize Daily: 5-7 Year Olds
programme.desc: Learn how to use subordinating conjunctions.

programme.title: Hey You What If?
programme.desc: To throw a ball around the world, you need to start out in space, throw it ten times the speed of a bullet and make sure your ball does not explode when it hits the atmosphere.

programme.title: Horrible Histories
programme.desc: The Vikings launch their advert for We Sell Any Monk, Queen Elizabeth I surprises her court with some very odd laws, the sacrifice-obsessed Aztec priests sing their gruesome disco song, plus the Roman equivalent of text messaging.

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Steve Backshall and his long-suffering crew return for more deadly encounters with animals hoping to earn a place on his hallowed Deadly 60 list. Steve Backshall travels to Indonesia in search of three very different reptiles to add to his list of 60 deadly predators. He and his crew have a nerve-racking close encounter when they are chased by a group of ravenous, three-metre-long komodo dragons, the world's largest venomous lizards! Steve also demonstrates the incredible gliding technique of a tiny flying lizard and heads out on a nocturnal hunt for the beautiful but lethal green pit viper.

programme.title: Operation Ouch!
programme.desc: The doctors get competitive in a race to reveal what happens when blood vessels get blocked, Dr Xand goes for some physiotherapy and Dr Chris is out with the emergency services helping a man with chest pain. Meanwhile, in accident and emergency, one patient has hurt his neck playing rugby and another has cut his head being a superhero.

programme.title: Go Get Arty
programme.desc: It's kids v parents! The Kwapongs make smashable pinatas and remix classic art in Liverpool. Maisie Adam draws a footballing narwhal, and an illusion artist makes her face vanish.

programme.title: Out of This World
programme.desc: In this episode, Dr Maggie reveals the game changers of space missions and spacecraft, from the space shuttle to the Hubble Space Telescope, that have transformed our lives on Earth and beyond. Dr Maggie’s star guest is Nasa astronaut Kathy Sullivan, who is a game changer herself. She flew in the space shuttle three times, delivered Hubble into orbit and was the first American woman to walk in space! Dr Maggie also counts down the Top 5 Most Expensive Missions and all your space questions are answered in Ask Maggie. Buckle up, it’s time to go Out of This World!

programme.title: The Dengineers
programme.desc: Siblings Nethuni and Abheetha are obsessed with optical illusions and want a den where they can work together to create new tricks to dazzle their friends.

programme.title: One Zoo Three
programme.desc: Cam, Tyler and Aaron want to hold a superhero-themed party inspired by the secret superpowers of some of the zoo’s most incredible animals. Rica the armadillo comes out of her shell to show off her super-sensitive sniff, and Moby the eagle owl performs awesome aerobatics without making a sound. Meanwhile, Bactrian camels Mo and Navas display some serious suction with their super-slurping, and Cletus the dwarf crocodile arrives at the zoo ready to flex his pecs. Aaron reveals the mighty powers of the cockroach, and the brothers take a trip to Uganda to help a conservation project caring for orphaned chimpanzees.

programme.title: Our School
programme.desc: Year 8 dive into a deep-water challenge, learning how to save lives in just six lessons. For Sean, it’s a chance to help him concentrate better, while Mary hopes to improve her confidence.

programme.title: Gym Stars
programme.desc: The rhythmic girls are off on a beach clean, while Winston competes in France.

programme.title: Octonauts
programme.desc: Join an adventurous team of underwater explorers as they dive into action, rescuing all sorts of amazing sea creatures and trying their best to protect the ocean.

programme.title: Big Lizard
programme.desc: Cosima takes over Dad's mission to film a unique underwater plant. But his special camera proves harder to operate than she'd thought, and Big Lizard keeps getting distracted.

programme.title: Piripenguins
programme.desc: Nugget joins the Piripenguin Dance Club and grabs the glory with Pancake’s signature move – until she’s challenged to create her own dance and ends up needing her friend’s help.

programme.title: Duck and Frog

programme.title: Red Riding Hood
programme.desc: Young Valerie (Amanda Seyfried) feels torn between two men. She loves Peter, but her parents intend that she marry wealthy Henry. Valerie and Peter are going to run away together, but her sister is killed by a werewolf before they can put their plan into action. The villagers call on the help of Father Solomon (Gary Oldman), a famous monster hunter who warns that the beast takes human form by day. Then Valerie suspects that the werewolf is someone she loves.

programme.title: Dim Sum Funeral
programme.desc: In the wake of her death, the embittered children of Chinese-American matriarch Mrs. Xiao (Lisa Lu) begrudgingly return to their childhood home for a bristly -- and brief, they hope -- reunion. But after Xiao's maid and sole confidant, Viola (Talia Shire), reveals her wish to undergo a week-long Buddhist funeral rite, the younger Xiaos -- including plastic surgeon Alexander (Russell Wong) and lesbian actress Meimei (Steph Song) -- have seven days to come to terms with her death, and each other.

programme.title: Parental Guidance
programme.desc: Minor-league baseball announcer Artie Decker (Billy Crystal) and his wife, Diane (Bette Midler), get to see their only child, Alice (Marisa Tomei), very seldom. To their surprise, Alice and her husband (Tom Everett Scott) ask them to watch their children so they can embark on a trip for work. It promises to be a fun time for all, until the three young ones turn out to be quite a handful for this old-fashioned couple. Artie and Diane may need to bend the rules to make everyone happy in the end.

programme.title: Love, Simon
programme.desc: Everyone deserves a great love story, but for 17-year-old Simon Spier, it's a little more complicated. He hasn't told his family or friends that he's gay, and he doesn't know the identity of the anonymous classmate that he's fallen for online. Resolving both issues proves hilarious, terrifying and life-changing.

programme.title: The Judge
programme.desc: Hank Palmer (Robert Downey Jr.), a brilliant but shady attorney, returns to his Indiana hometown after learning that his mother has passed away. His arrival triggers renewed tension between himself and his father, Judge Joseph Palmer (Robert Duvall), who makes no secret of his disapproval of Hank's morally ambiguous career. As the lawyer prepares to depart, his father is arrested for a hit-and-run death. Hank takes on his father's defense, despite the objections of the resentful old man.

programme.title: Man Down
programme.desc: When U.S. Marine Gabriel Drummer (Shia LaBeouf) returns from Afghanistan, he finds the place he once called home is no better than the battlefields he fought on overseas. Accompanied by his best friend, a hard-nosed Marine whose natural instinct is to shoot first and ask questions later, Gabriel searches desperately for his estranged son and his wife, leading to a suspect who has vital information about their location.

programme.title: The Hitcher
programme.desc: While transporting a car from Chicago to San Diego, Jim Halsey (C. Thomas Howell) picks up a hitchhiker named John Ryder (Rutger Hauer), who claims to be a serial killer. After a daring escape, Jim hopes to never see Ryder again. But when he witnesses the hitchhiker murdering an entire family, Jim pursues Ryder with the help of truck-stop waitress Nash (Jennifer Jason Leigh), pitting the rivals against each other in a deadly series of car chases and brutal murders.

programme.title: Pacific Rim Uprising
programme.desc: Jake Pentecost is a once-promising Jaeger pilot whose legendary father gave his life to secure humanity's victory against the monstrous Kaiju. Jake has since abandoned his training only to become caught up in a criminal underworld. But when an even more unstoppable threat is unleashed to tear through cities and bring the world to its knees, Jake is given one last chance by his estranged sister, Mako Mori, to live up to his father's legacy.

programme.title: The Blair Witch Project
programme.desc: Found video footage tells the tale of three film students (Heather Donahue, Joshua Leonard, Michael C. Williams) who've traveled to a small town to collect documentary footage about the Blair Witch, a legendary local murderer. Over the course of several days, the students interview townspeople and gather clues to support the tale's veracity. But the project takes a frightening turn when the students lose their way in the woods and begin hearing horrific noises.

programme.title: Book of Shadows: Blair Witch 2
programme.desc: As it follows the twisted path traveled by five people fixated on "The Blair Witch Project," "Book of Shadows: Blair Witch 2" journeys into a dark and dangerous place where the line between truth and fiction blurs and perhaps vanishes altogether. Individual perception grows increasingly untrustworthy as the film's protagonists find themselves caught in a vortex of unspeakable evil, the origins of which -- human or supernatural -- remain chillingly uncertain.

programme.title: Blair Witch
programme.desc: A young man and his friends venture into the Black Hills Forest in Maryland to uncover the mystery surrounding his missing sister. Many believe her disappearance 17 years earlier is connected to the legend of the Blair Witch. At first the group is hopeful, especially when two locals act as guides through the dark and winding woods. As the night wears on, a visit from a menacing presence soon makes them realize that the legend is all too real, and more sinister than they could have ever imagined.

programme.title: Scanners
programme.desc: Scanners are men and women born with incredible telepathic and telekinetic powers. There are many who exercise the benefits of their special gifts in a safe and judicious manner. However, there is a group of renegade scanners who plan to create a race that will rule the world.

programme.title: Shut In
programme.desc: Mary Portman is a widowed child psychologist who lives in isolation in rural Maine. The horrific car accident that killed her husband also left her 18-year-old stepson Stephen in a bedridden, catatonic state, leaving him completely dependent on her. When one of Portman's young patients vanishes without a trace, she becomes convinced that the boy's ghost is now in the house as a dangerous ice storm starts to wreak havoc outside.

programme.title: Full Metal Jacket
programme.desc: Stanley Kubrick's take on the Vietnam War follows smart-aleck Private Davis (Matthew Modine), quickly christened "Joker" by his foul-mouthed drill sergeant (R. Lee Ermey), and pudgy Private Lawrence (Vincent D'Onofrio), nicknamed "Gomer Pyle," as they endure the rigors of basic training. Though Pyle takes a frightening detour, Joker graduates to the Marine Corps and is sent to Vietnam as a journalist, covering -- and eventually participating in -- the bloody Battle of Hué.

programme.title: Our Kind of Traitor
programme.desc: A money launderer (Stellan Skarsgard) for Russian gangsters asks a couple vacationing in Marrakech, Morocco, to deliver incriminating evidence to an MI6 agent (Damian Lewis).

programme.title: DC League of Super-Pets
programme.desc: Krypto the Super-Dog and Superman are inseparable best friends, sharing the same superpowers and fighting crime side by side in Metropolis. However, when the Man of Steel and the rest of the Justice League are kidnapped, Krypto must convince a ragtag group of animals to master their own newfound powers for a rescue mission.

programme.title: Just Friends
programme.desc: High school student Chris Brander (Ryan Reynolds) loves his best friend, Jamie Palamino (Amy Smart). He finally confesses his feelings, but she tells him that she just wants to be friends, and he leaves town in shame. Ten years later, Chris is a successful record executive and involved with self-absorbed pop star Samantha James (Anna Faris). He still pines for Jamie, though, and when his plans to go to Paris for the holidays fall through, he returns to his hometown to try and win her heart.

programme.title: Joshy
programme.desc: Four months after the suicide of his fiancée (Alison Brie), a man (Thomas Middleditch) and his buddies (Adam Pally, Alex Ross Perry) decide to move forward with plans for a wild bachelor party.

programme.title: The Lobster
programme.desc: In a dystopian society, single people must find a mate within 45 days or be transformed into an animal of their choice.

programme.title: Aniara
programme.desc: When a spacecraft carrying settlers to Mars strays off course, the consumption-obsessed passengers are prompted to consider their place in the universe.

programme.title: The Shape of Water
programme.desc: Elisa is a mute, isolated woman who works in a hidden, high-security government laboratory. Her life changes forever when she discovers the lab's classified secret -- a mysterious, scaled creature from South America that lives in a water tank.

programme.title: Birds of Prey (and the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)
programme.desc: It's open season on Harley Quinn when her explosive breakup with the Joker puts a big fat target on her back. Unprotected and on the run, Quinn faces the wrath of narcissistic crime boss Black Mask, his right-hand man, Victor Zsasz, and every other thug in the city. But things soon even out for Harley when she becomes unexpected allies with three deadly women -- Huntress, Black Canary and Renee Montoya.

programme.title: Men
programme.desc: Harper retreats to the countryside to be alone in the wake of a tragedy, but her unease at the town's leering and uncannily similar men grows into a fully fledged nightmare as her arrival awakens something primal in the forest.

programme.title: Body at Brighton Rock
programme.desc: Wendy, a part-time summer employee at a mountainous state park, takes on a rough trail assignment at the end of the season, trying to prove to her friends that she's capable enough to do the job. When she takes a wrong turn and ends up deep in the backcountry, she stumbles upon what might be a potential crime scene. Stuck with no communication after losing her radio and with orders to guard the site, Wendy must fight the urge to run and do the harder job of staying put.

programme.title: My Soul to Take
programme.desc: In the small town of Riverton, a local legend tells of a serial killer's oath to come back and kill the seven children who were born on the night he supposedly died. Now 16 years later, Riverton residents are disappearing again, making some wonder if the legend is true. Bug (Max Thieriot), plagued by nightmares all his life, is one of the so-called Riverton Seven, and it's up to him to save his friends from an evil that will not rest.

programme.title: Hail Satan?
programme.desc: Lucien Greaves co-founds the Satanic Temple, a religious movement that calls for a revolution to save the nation's soul.

programme.title: Abraham Lincoln: Vampire Hunter
programme.desc: While still a boy, Abraham Lincoln loses his mother to a vampire's bite. He vows revenge, but fails in the attempt, narrowly escaping with his life. He is rescued by Henry (Dominic Cooper), a charismatic vampire hunter who instructs Abe in the fine art of dispatching bloodsuckers. Abe (Benjamin Walker) continues his fight against the undead well into adulthood and his presidency, making a last stand against the ultimate vampire foe (Rufus Sewell) on the eve of the Civil War's defining battle.

programme.title: Trance
programme.desc: Simon (James McAvoy), a fine-art auctioneer, joins a gang of thieves led by Franck (Vincent Cassel) to steal a priceless Goya painting. During the heist Simon suffers a head injury and awakes with no memory of where he hid the artwork. When torture and physical threats fail to break through his amnesia, Franck hires a hypnotherapist named Elizabeth (Rosario Dawson) to find the answer. But as Elizabeth probes the recesses of Simon's mind, the lines between truth and deceit start to blur.

programme.title: The Whistlers
programme.desc: A Romanian police officer, determined to free from prison a crooked businessman who knows where a mobster's money is hidden, must learn the difficult ancestral language used on the island of Gomera.

programme.title: The Way, Way Back
programme.desc: Duncan (Liam James) is an awkward teen who must spend the summer at a beach house with his mother (Toni Collette), her boyfriend, Trent (Steve Carell), and Trent's obnoxious daughter. Trent can't resist badgering Duncan, so the youth steals away to a water park and gets a job that will help him stay off Trent's radar. As Duncan tends to the slides and pools of the aging park, he finds a father figure in wisecracking park manager Owen (Sam Rockwell) at a time when he desperately needs one.

programme.title: Monster-in-Law
programme.desc: Charlotte (Jennifer Lopez) is smitten when she meets Dr. Kevin Fields (Michael Vartan). So when Kevin pops the question after they start dating, Charlotte happily accepts. But she soon realizes that Kevin's mom, Viola (Jane Fonda), is not quite thrilled to have a new family member. Viola, a newscaster, has just lost her job and is feeling rather attached to Kevin, so she regards Charlotte as her new competition -- and will apparently do anything to make her son call off the wedding.

programme.title: Won't Back Down
programme.desc: Jamie Fitzpatrick and Nona Alberts are two women from opposite sides of the social and economic track, but they have one thing in common: a mission to fix their community's broken school and ensure a bright future for their children. The two women refuse to let any obstacles stand in their way as they battle a bureaucracy that's hopelessly mired in traditional thinking, and they seek to re-energize a faculty that has lost its passion for teaching.

programme.title: The Town
programme.desc: Doug MacRay leads a band of ruthless bank robbers and has no real attachments except for James, who -- despite his dangerous temper -- is like a brother. Everything changes for Doug when James briefly takes a hostage, bank employee Claire Keesey. Learning that she lives in the gang's neighborhood, Doug seeks her out to discover what she knows, and he falls in love. As the romance deepens, he wants out of his criminal life, but that could threaten Claire.

programme.title: Megan Leavey
programme.desc: The true life story of Megan Leavey, a young Marine corporal whose unique discipline and bond with a military combat dog saved many lives during her deployment in Iraq. Assigned to clean up the K-9 unit after a disciplinary hearing, Leavey starts to identify with Rex, a particularly aggressive dog that she trains. Over the course of their service, Megan and Rex complete more than 100 missions until an improvised explosive device injures both, putting their fates in jeopardy.

programme.title: Mickey 17
programme.desc: A disposable employee is sent on a human expedition to colonize the ice world Niflheim. After one iteration dies, a new body is regenerated with most of his memories intact.

programme.title: Companion
programme.desc: A weekend getaway at a remote cabin turns to chaos when it's revealed that one of the guests -- a subservient android built for human companionship -- has gone haywire.

programme.title: Star Wars: The Phantom Menace
programme.desc: Obi-Wan Kenobi (Ewan McGregor) is a young apprentice Jedi knight under the tutelage of Qui-Gon Jinn (Liam Neeson) ; Anakin Skywalker (Jake Lloyd), who will later father Luke Skywalker and become known as Darth Vader, is just a 9-year-old boy. When the Trade Federation cuts off all routes to the planet Naboo, Qui-Gon and Obi-Wan are assigned to settle the matter.

programme.title: Star Wars: Attack of the Clones
programme.desc: Set ten years after the events of "The Phantom Menace," the Republic continues to be mired in strife and chaos. A separatist movement encompassing hundreds of planets and powerful corporate alliances poses new threats to the galaxy that even the Jedi cannot stem. These moves, long planned by an as yet unrevealed and powerful force, lead to the beginning of the Clone Wars -- and the beginning of the end of the Republic.

programme.title: Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith
programme.desc: It has been three years since the Clone Wars began. Jedi Master Obi-Wan Kenobi (Ewan McGregor) and Jedi Knight Anakin Skywalker (Hayden Christensen) rescue Chancellor Palpatine (Ian McDiarmid) from General Grievous, the commander of the droid armies, but Grievous escapes. Suspicions are raised within the Jedi Council concerning Chancellor Palpatine, with whom Anakin has formed a bond. Asked to spy on the chancellor, and full of bitterness toward the Jedi Council, Anakin embraces the Dark Side.

programme.title: Star Wars: A New Hope
programme.desc: The Imperial Forces -- under orders from cruel Darth Vader (David Prowse) -- hold Princess Leia (Carrie Fisher) hostage, in their efforts to quell the rebellion against the Galactic Empire. Luke Skywalker (Mark Hamill) and Han Solo (Harrison Ford), captain of the Millennium Falcon, work together with the companionable droid duo R2-D2 (Kenny Baker) and C-3PO (Anthony Daniels) to rescue the beautiful princess, help the Rebel Alliance, and restore freedom and justice to the Galaxy.

programme.title: Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back
programme.desc: The adventure continues in this "Star Wars" sequel. Luke Skywalker (Mark Hamill), Han Solo (Harrison Ford), Princess Leia (Carrie Fisher) and Chewbacca (Peter Mayhew) face attack by the Imperial forces and its AT-AT walkers on the ice planet Hoth. While Han and Leia escape in the Millennium Falcon, Luke travels to Dagobah in search of Yoda. Only with the Jedi master's help will Luke survive when the dark side of the Force beckons him into the ultimate duel with Darth Vader (David Prowse).

programme.title: Star Wars: Return of the Jedi
programme.desc: Luke Skywalker (Mark Hamill) battles horrible Jabba the Hutt and cruel Darth Vader to save his comrades in the Rebel Alliance and triumph over the Galactic Empire. Han Solo (Harrison Ford) and Princess Leia (Carrie Fisher) reaffirm their love and team with Chewbacca, Lando Calrissian (Billy Dee Williams), the Ewoks and the androids C-3PO and R2-D2 to aid in the disruption of the Dark Side and the defeat of the evil emperor.

programme.title: The Mummy
programme.desc: Nick Morton is a soldier of fortune who plunders ancient sites for timeless artifacts and sells them to the highest bidder. When Nick and his partner come under attack in the Middle East, the ensuing battle accidentally unearths Ahmanet, a betrayed Egyptian princess who was entombed under the desert for thousands of years. With her powers constantly evolving, Morton must now stop the resurrected monster as she embarks on a furious rampage through the streets of London.

programme.title: Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl
programme.desc: Capt. Jack Sparrow (Johnny Depp) arrives at Port Royal in the Caribbean without a ship or crew. His timing is inopportune, however, because later that evening the town is besieged by a pirate ship. The pirates kidnap the governor's daughter, Elizabeth (Keira Knightley), who's in possession of a valuable coin that is linked to a curse that has transformed the pirates into the undead. A gallant blacksmith (Orlando Bloom) in love with Elizabeth allies with Sparrow in pursuit of the pirates.

programme.title: Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Man's Chest
programme.desc: When ghostly pirate Davy Jones comes to collect a blood debt, Capt. Jack Sparrow must find a way to avoid his fate lest his soul be damned for all time. Nevertheless, the wily ghost manages to interrupt the wedding plans of Jack's friends Will Turner and Elizabeth Swann.

programme.title: Pirates of the Caribbean: At World's End
programme.desc: Will Turner (Orlando Bloom) and Elizabeth Swann (Keira Knightley) join forces with Capt. Barbossa (Geoffrey Rush) to free Jack Sparrow (Johnny Depp) from Davy Jones' locker. Meanwhile, the crew of the Flying Dutchman ghost ship wreaks havoc on the Seven Seas. The friends must navigate dangerous waters to confront Chinese pirate Sao Feng (Chow Yun-Fat) and, ultimately, they must choose sides in a battle wherein the pirate life hangs in the balance.

programme.title: Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Men Tell No Tales
programme.desc: Thrust into an all-new adventure, a down-on-his-luck Capt. Jack Sparrow feels the winds of ill-fortune blowing even more strongly when deadly ghost sailors led by his old nemesis, the evil Capt. Salazar, escape from the Devil's Triangle. Jack's only hope of survival lies in seeking out the legendary Trident of Poseidon, but to find it, he must forge an uneasy alliance with a brilliant and beautiful astronomer and a headstrong young man in the British navy.

programme.title: Pirates of the Caribbean: On Stranger Tides
programme.desc: The checkered past of Capt. Jack Sparrow (Johnny Depp) catches up to him when he encounters Angelica (Penélope Cruz), a beautiful pirate that Jack once loved then left. Angelica forces him to accompany her to the Queen Anne's Revenge, the ship of the notorious Blackbeard (Ian McShane). Accompanied by a zombie crew, the trio sets sail to find the legendary Fountain of Youth. However, Jack's rival, Barbossa (Geoffrey Rush), also seeks the fountain, as does a ship from Spain.

programme.title: The Unholy
programme.desc: A girl inexplicably gains the power to heal the sick after a supposed visitation from the Virgin Mary. As word spreads and people flock to witness her miracles, a disgraced journalist visits the small New England town to investigate. However, when strange events start happening, he soon questions if these phenomena are the works of the Virgin Mary or something more sinister.
